translations.literal: Yuele's sons Wu'erzhan and grandsons Sehengtu and others showed resentment in word and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele's sons Wu'erzhan and grandsons Sehengtu and others showed resentment in word and countenance.

sentences.zh: 廉親王允禩又復逞其離間，肆為讒言。

translations.literal: Prince Lian Yunsi again indulged his sowing of discord and recklessly spoke slander.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lian Yunsi again indulged his sowing of discord and recklessly spoke slander.

sentences.zh: 安郡王爵不准承襲。

translations.literal: The title of Prince An may not be inherited.
translations.idiomatic: The title of Prince An may not be inherited.

sentences.zh: 」乾隆四十三年，高宗以阿巴泰、岳樂屢著功績，封華玘孫奇昆輔國公，世襲。

translations.literal: " In the forty-third year of Qianlong the Gaozong Emperor, because Abatai and Yuele had repeatedly achieved merit, enfeoffed Hua Qi's grandson Qikun as Duke Fuguo, inheritable in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: " In Qianlong 43 the Gaozong Emperor, because Abatai and Yuele had repeatedly achieved merit, enfeoffed Hua Qi's grandson Qikun as Duke Fuguo, inheritable in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 溫良貝子博和託，阿巴泰第二子。

translations.literal: Beizi Wenliang Bohetuo was Abatai's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Bohetuo, posthumously beizi Wenliang, was Abatai's second son.

sentences.zh: 初封輔國公。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從徵北韓，圍南漢山城，偕尼堪擊走其援兵，斬殪甚眾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed the campaign against Korea, besieged Namhansanseong, and together with Ni Kan drove off the relief army and killed and destroyed very many.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he followed the campaign against Korea, besieged Namhansanseong, and together with Ni Kan drove off the relief army and killed and destroyed very many.

sentences.zh: 三年，從伐明，自董家口略明都西南六府，入山西界。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed in attacking the Ming, from Dongjiakou raided the six prefectures southwest of the Ming capital, and entered Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 3 he followed in attacking the Ming, from Dongjiakou raided the six prefectures southwest of the Ming capital, and entered Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 移師克濟南。

translations.literal: Shifting the army he took Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Shifting the army he took Jinan.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜銀二千。

translations.literal: When the army returned, two thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, two thousand taels of silver were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 七年，從阿巴泰伐明，自黃崖口入。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Abatai in campaigning against the Ming and entered through Huangyakou.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 7 he followed Abatai in campaigning against the Ming and entered through Huangyakou.

sentences.zh: 及還，賜銀三千。

translations.literal: On his return three thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: On his return three thousand taels of silver were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關，破李自成，進貝子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed in entering the Pass, defeated Li Zicheng, and was advanced to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he followed in entering the Pass, defeated Li Zicheng, and was advanced to beizi.

sentences.zh: 三年，從多鐸擊喀爾喀蘇尼特部騰機思、騰機特等。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Dodo in attacking the Khalkha Sunite chieftains Tengjisi, Tengjite, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he followed Dodo in attacking the Khalkha Sunite chieftains Tengjisi, Tengjite, and others.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，卒，予謚。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year he died; a posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Shunzhi 5 he died; a posthumous title was granted.

sentences.zh: 子六，彰泰，襲貝子。

translations.literal: He had six sons; Zhangtai inherited the beizi title.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons; Zhangtai inherited the beizi title.

sentences.zh: 彰泰襲爵，進封。

translations.literal: Zhangtai inherited the title and was advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangtai inherited the title and was advanced in rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年春，吳三桂陷湖南，上命貝勒尚善為大將軍，率師下岳州，以彰泰參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year of Kangxi, Wu Sangui seized Hunan; the emperor appointed beile Shangshan grand general, led an army down to Yuezhou, and made Zhangtai deputy in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Kangxi 13, Wu Sangui seized Hunan; the emperor appointed beile Shangshan grand general, led an army down to Yuezhou, and made Zhangtai deputy in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詔責行師延緩。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year an edict rebuked the delay in marching.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15 an edict rebuked the delay in marching.

sentences.zh: 彰泰與尚善議水陸併進，遣額司泰等破敵洞庭湖，獲舟五十餘。

translations.literal: Zhangtai and Shangshan planned a joint advance by land and water, sent Esitai and others to defeat the enemy on Dongting Lake, and captured more than fifty boats.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangtai and Shangshan planned a joint advance by land and water, sent Esitai and others to defeat the enemy on Dongting Lake, and captured more than fifty boats.

sentences.zh: 敵立椿套湖峽口阻我師。

translations.literal: The enemy erected stakes at the lake gorge mouth of Taohu to block our army.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy erected stakes at the Taohu lake gorge mouth to block our army.

sentences.zh: 十七年，督兵伐椿，棹輕舟破敵柳林嘴，發炮毀其船。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he supervised troops in attacking the stakes, rowed light boats to defeat the enemy at Liulinzui, and fired cannon to destroy their ships.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 he supervised troops in attacking the stakes, rowed light boats to defeat the enemy at Liulinzui, and fired cannon to destroy their ships.

sentences.zh: 八月，尚善卒於軍，貝勒察尼代為大將軍，授彰泰撫遠將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Shangshan died in the army; beile Cha Ni replaced him as grand general and Zhangtai was appointed Pacification General for the Distant Regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shangshan died in the army; beile Cha Ni replaced him as grand general and Zhangtai was appointed Pacification General for the Distant Regions.

sentences.zh: 九月，督兵出南津港。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he supervised troops out of Nanjingang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he supervised troops out of Nanjingang.

sentences.zh: 十月，破敵陸石口，屯白米灘，絕三桂兵運道。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he defeated the enemy at Lushikou, encamped at Baimitan, and cut Sangui's army supply route.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he defeated the enemy at Lushikou, encamped at Baimitan, and cut Sangui's army supply route.

sentences.zh: 十八年，三桂將陳珀等以乏食出降，吳應麒走衡州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Sangui's generals Chen Bo and others, short of food, came over; Wu Yingqi fled to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 Sangui's generals Chen Bo and others, short of food, surrendered; Wu Yingqi fled to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 都統珠滿等克湘陰，彰泰克華容、石首。

translations.literal: Commander-in-chief Zhuman and others took Xiangyin; Zhangtai took Huarong and Shishou.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief Zhuman and others took Xiangyin; Zhangtai took Huarong and Shishou.

sentences.zh: 會安親王岳樂復長沙，簡親王喇布復衡州，詔彰泰與會師。

translations.literal: When Prince An Yuele recovered Changsha and Prince Jian Labu recovered Hengzhou, an edict ordered Zhangtai to join forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince An Yuele recovered Changsha and Prince Jian Labu recovered Hengzhou, an edict ordered Zhangtai to join forces.

sentences.zh: 自衡州進攻武岡，擊破三桂將吳國貴等。

translations.literal: From Hengzhou he advanced to attack Wugang and defeated Sangui's generals Wu Guogui and others.
translations.idiomatic: From Hengzhou he advanced to attack Wugang and defeated Sangui's generals Wu Guogui and others.

sentences.zh: 十一月，召岳樂還京師，命彰泰代為定遠平寇大將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Yuele was recalled to the capital and Zhangtai was ordered to replace him as Pacification Commissioner General for the Distant Pacification of Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yuele was recalled to the capital and Zhangtai was ordered to replace him as Pacification Commissioner General for the Distant Pacification of Bandits.

sentences.zh: 十九年，復沅州，靖州，三桂所置綏寧諸將吏及附近土司俱降。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he recovered Yuanzhou and Jingzhou; the generals, officials, and nearby tribal chiefs that Sangui had installed in Suining and elsewhere all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 he recovered Yuanzhou and Jingzhou; the generals, officials, and nearby tribal chiefs that Sangui had installed in Suining and elsewhere all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「將軍蔡毓榮調遣漢兵，今進取貴州，若不相聞，恐礙事機。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "General Cai Yurong is deploying Han troops; he is now advancing on Guizhou; if we are not kept informed, I fear the timing of operations will be hindered.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "General Cai Yurong is deploying Han troops and is now advancing on Guizhou; if we are not kept informed, I fear operations will be hindered.

sentences.zh: 」詔毓榮軍事關白大將軍。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered that Yurong's military affairs be reported to the grand general.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered that Yurong's military affairs be reported to the grand general.

sentences.zh: 十月，次鎮遠，遣兵攻鎮遠關，截其隘，而與毓榮督兵躪敵壘。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he halted at Zhenyuan, dispatched troops to attack Zhenyuan Pass, cut off its defile, and together with Yurong directed troops in overrunning the enemy stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he halted at Zhenyuan, sent forces against Zhenyuan Pass to seal its chokepoint, and with Cai Yurong personally directed the overrunning of the enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 所遣兵亦奪十向口，破敵大岩門，逐之至偏橋衛，遂復鎮遠。

translations.literal: The troops he dispatched also seized Shixiangkou, broke the enemy Great Rock Gate, pursued them to Pianqiao Guard, and thus recovered Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His detached column also took Shixiangkou, stormed the enemy’s Great Rock Gate, drove them to Pianqiao Guard, and recovered Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 進下平越及新添衛，趨貴陽。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Pingyue and Xintian Guard, pressing toward Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched down through Pingyue and Xintian Guard and pressed on Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 三桂孫世璠及應麒等俱走還雲南。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's grandson Shi Fan and Yingqi and the rest all fled back to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui’s grandson Shi Fan, Wu Yingqi, and the others all fled back toward Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 迭克安順、石阡、都勻、思南諸府。

translations.literal: In succession he captured Anshun, Shiqian, Duyun, Sinan, and the other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: One after another he took Anshun, Shiqian, Duyun, Sinan, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十一月，復永寧，破敵安籠鋪，逐之至雞公背山鐵索橋，師駐貴陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he recovered Yongning, routed the enemy at Anlong post, pursued them to the chain bridge at Jigongbei Mountain, and the army encamped at Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he retook Yongning, smashed the enemy at Anlong post, pursued them to the chain bridge at Jigongbei Mountain, and encamped at Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 詔趣彰泰進規雲南。

translations.literal: An edict urged Zhangtai to advance and plan the conquest of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pressed Zhangtai to press the campaign against Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 二十年正月，渡盤江，破敵沙子哨，進次臘茄坡，復新興所，逐北三十里，克普安、霑益。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twentieth year he crossed the Pan River, defeated the enemy at Shazi post, advanced and halted at Lajia Slope, recovered Xinxing subprefecture, pursued north thirty li, and captured Pu'an and Zhanyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kangxi 20 he crossed the Pan River, routed the enemy at Shazi post, halted at Lajia Slope, retook Xinxing subprefecture, pursued thirty li north, and seized Pu’an and Zhanyi.

sentences.zh: 大將軍賚塔自廣西入曲靖，會於嵩明州，合圍雲南會城，距三十里。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Laita entered Qujing from Guangxi; they met at Songming Prefecture, combined to invest the Yunnan capital, and encamped thirty li away.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Laita came up from Guangxi through Qujing; the two armies joined at Songming and together invested the Yunnan capital, thirty li from the walls.

sentences.zh: 世璠將胡國柄、劉起龍等以萬餘人列象陣拒戰。

translations.literal: Shi Fan's generals Hu Guobing, Liu Qilong, and others drew up an elephant formation with more than ten thousand men to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Fan’s generals Hu Guobing and Liu Qilong fielded more than ten thousand men in an elephant line to block the advance.

sentences.zh: 賚塔軍其右，彰泰軍其左，自卯達午，殊死戰，破敵陣，斬國柄、起龍等，俘獲無算。

translations.literal: Laita's army was on the right, Zhangtai's on the left; from the mao hour until noon they fought desperately, broke the enemy formation, beheaded Guobing, Qilong, and the rest, and took captives beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Laita took the right wing and Zhangtai the left; from dawn until noon they fought hand to hand, broke the enemy line, slew Guobing and Qilong, and took captives beyond count.

sentences.zh: 令諸軍分扼南壩、薩石衛、走馬街、雙塔寺、得勝橋、重關諸地，於是大理、臨安、永順、姚安、武定世璠所置將吏，相繼詣軍前降。

translations.literal: He ordered the armies to hold separately Nanba, Sashi Guard, Zoumajie, Shuangta Temple, Desheng Bridge, Chongguan, and other places; thereupon the officers Shi Fan had placed in Dali, Lin'an, Yongshun, Yao'an, and Wuding came in succession to the camps to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He posted detachments at Nanba, Sashi Guard, Zoumajie, Shuangta Temple, Desheng Bridge, Chongguan, and other crossings; then the garrisons Shi Fan had left in Dali, Lin’an, Yongshun, Yao’an, and Wuding came over one after another.

sentences.zh: 世璠將馬寶、胡國柱等自四川，夏國相自廣西，還救雲南，彰泰遣兵迎擊，寶次姚安，亦乞降。

translations.literal: Shi Fan's generals Ma Bao and Hu Guozhu from Sichuan and Xia Guoxiang from Guangxi returned to rescue Yunnan; Zhangtai sent troops to meet and attack them; Bao halted at Yao'an and also petitioned to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Bao and Hu Guozhu marched down from Sichuan and Xia Guoxiang from Guangxi to relieve Yunnan; Zhangtai met them in the field, and Bao, halted at Yao’an, sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 國柱走鶴慶、麗江，希福攻雲龍州，國柱自經死。

translations.literal: Guozhu fled toward Heqing and Lijiang; Xifu attacked Yunlong Prefecture; Guozhu hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhu fled toward Heqing and Lijiang; Xifu struck Yunlong Prefecture, and Guozhu hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 國相走廣西，李國樑等圍之西板橋，國相亦降，與寶同檻送京師。

translations.literal: Guoxiang fled to Guangxi; Li Guoliang and others surrounded him at Xibanqiao; Guoxiang also surrendered and, together with Bao, was sent to the capital in a caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxiang fled into Guangxi; Li Guoliang cornered him at Xibanqiao, and he too surrendered; he and Bao were sent to the capital in the same prisoner cart.

sentences.zh: 將軍趙良棟師自四川至，彰泰偕賚塔及良棟等屢破敵南壩、得勝橋、太平橋、走馬街諸地。

translations.literal: General Zhao Liangdong's army arrived from Sichuan; Zhangtai together with Laita and Liangdong repeatedly defeated the enemy at Nanba, Desheng Bridge, Taiping Bridge, Zoumajie, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhao Liangdong’s column arrived from Sichuan; with Laita and Liangdong, Zhangtai repeatedly broke the enemy at Nanba, Desheng Bridge, Taiping Bridge, Zoumajie, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 師薄城環攻，世璠自經死，其將何進忠等出降。

translations.literal: The army pressed against the city and invested it on all sides; Shi Fan hanged himself; his generals He Jinzhong and others came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The armies closed on the walls; Shi Fan hanged himself, and his generals He Jinzhong and the rest came out to yield.

sentences.zh: 彰泰戒將士毋殺掠，入城安撫，收倉庫，戮世璠屍，函首獻闕下。

translations.literal: Zhangtai warned the troops not to kill or plunder; entered the city to reassure the people; seized the storehouses; dismembered Shi Fan's corpse; and sent the head in a casket to present below the imperial gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangtai forbade killing and looting, entered to pacify the city, secured the granaries, dismembered Shi Fan’s corpse, and sent his head to the capital in a casket.

sentences.zh: 雲南平。

translations.literal: Yunnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 授左宗正。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Clan Chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Clan Chieftain.

sentences.zh: 二十一年十月，師還，上迎勞盧溝橋南二十里。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-first year the army returned; the emperor came out twenty li south of the Lugou Bridge to welcome and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 21 the army returned; the emperor met them twenty li south of the Lugou Bridge to welcome and reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，議初下岳州遷延罪，以功不坐。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the charge of delay in the initial descent on Yuezhou was considered; on account of his merit he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22 the old charge of sluggishness at Yuezhou was reviewed; his recent merit spared him punishment.

sentences.zh: 賜金二十、銀千。

translations.literal: He was granted twenty taels of gold and a thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He received twenty taels of gold and a thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，坐濫舉宗人府屬官，罷左宗正。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, for indiscriminate recommendation of clan-house officials, he was removed as Left Clan Chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 24 he was dismissed as Left Clan Chieftain for reckless nominations in the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 二十九年正月，卒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of Kangxi 29.

sentences.zh: 子屯珠，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: His son Tunzhu inherited the rank of Prince of the State Who Guards the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tunzhu inherited as Prince of the State Who Guards the Realm.

sentences.zh: 授左宗正、禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Clan Chieftain and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Clan Chieftain and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-seventh year.

sentences.zh: 贈貝子，謚恪敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of beizi and given the posthumous title Kemin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made a beizi with the posthumous title Kemin.

sentences.zh: 孫逢信，以輔國公世襲。

translations.literal: His grandson Fengxin inherited in perpetual succession as Duke Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Fengxin held the rank of Duke Fuguo in perpetual succession.

sentences.zh: 博洛，阿巴泰第三子。

translations.literal: Bolo was Abatai's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Bolo was the third son of Abatai.

sentences.zh: 天聰九年，從伐明，有功。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tiancong he followed the campaign against the Ming and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 9 he joined the campaign against the Ming and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，封貝子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he was enfeoffed as beizi.

sentences.zh: 二年，與議政。

translations.literal: In the second year he joined in deliberating government.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he joined the council of regents.

sentences.zh: 三年，授理藩院承政。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed chengzheng of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 從攻寧遠，趨中後所。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Ningyuan and pressed toward Zhonghousuo.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the assault on Ningyuan and pushed toward Zhonghousuo.

sentences.zh: 明將祖大壽襲我軍後，巴牙喇纛章京哈寧阿等與相持，博洛突前奮擊，大壽引卻。

translations.literal: The Ming general Zu Dashou attacked our rear; banner commanders Haningga and others held him in check; Bolo charged forward and struck fiercely; Dashou withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming general Zu Dashou struck the rear, Haningga and other commanders held the line; Bolo drove forward in a fierce charge and Dashou pulled back.

sentences.zh: 五年，從濟爾哈朗迎來歸蒙古蘇班岱，擊敗明兵，賜良馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Jirhalang to welcome the Mongol Subandai who had come over, defeated Ming troops, and was granted a fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he followed Jirhalang to receive the defector Subandai, routed Ming forces, and was rewarded with a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 尋與諸王更番圍錦州。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he joined the princes in rotating the siege of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then took turns with the other princes investing Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，洪承疇以十三萬人援錦州，博洛偕阿濟格擊之，至塔山，獲筆架山積粟；

translations.literal: In the sixth year Hong Chengchou came with a hundred and thirty thousand men to relieve Jinzhou; Bolo together with Ajige attacked them, reached Tashan, and seized the grain stored at Bijia Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Hong Chengchou marched to relieve Jinzhou with a hundred and thirty thousand men; Bolo and Ajige met them, reached Tashan, and seized the grain depot at Bijia Mountain;

sentences.zh: 又偕羅洛渾等設伏阿爾齋堡，擊敗明將王樸、吳三桂。

translations.literal: He also together with Rolohoan and others set an ambush at Arqi Fort, defeated the Ming generals Wang Pu and Wu Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: then with Rolohoan and others ambushed the Ming at Arqi Fort and routed Wang Pu and Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關，破李自成，進貝勒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the entry into the Pass, defeated Li Zicheng, and was advanced to beile.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he crossed into China, broke Li Zicheng, and was raised to beile.

sentences.zh: 從多鐸徵河南。

translations.literal: He followed Dodo in campaigning in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Dodo into Henan.

sentences.zh: 二年，破自成潼關。

translations.literal: In the second year he broke Zicheng at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he shattered Zicheng at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 多鐸南征，下江寧，分師之半授博洛，下常州、蘇州，趨杭州，屢敗明兵。

translations.literal: Dodo marched south, took Jiangning, and gave Bolo half the army; Bolo took Changzhou and Suzhou, pressed toward Hangzhou, and repeatedly defeated Ming troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Dodo turned south and took Jiangning, he gave Bolo half the army; Bolo seized Changzhou and Suzhou, pressed on Hangzhou, and repeatedly routed Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 師臨錢塘江岸，明兵以為江潮方盛，營且沒，會潮連日不至，明潞王常淓以杭州降，淮王常清亦自紹興降。

translations.literal: When the army reached the Qiantang River bank the Ming thought the tide was at flood and the camp would be drowned; but the tide failed for days on end; the Ming Prince of Lu Changfang surrendered Hangzhou, and the Prince of Huai Changqing also surrendered from Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the Qiantang the Ming expected the tide to sweep the camp away, but the waters stayed low for days; Prince Lu Changfang surrendered Hangzhou, and Prince Huai Changqing came in from Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 克嘉興，徇吳江，破明將吳易，攻江陰亦下。

translations.literal: He took Jiaxing, swept Wujiang, defeated the Ming general Wu Yi, and also took Jiangyin by assault.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jiaxing, raided Wujiang, defeated Wu Yi, and stormed Jiangyin as well.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜金二百、銀萬五千、鞍馬一。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was granted two hundred taels of gold, fifteen thousand taels of silver, and one saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he received two hundred taels of gold, fifteen thousand taels of silver, and a horse.

sentences.zh: 三年，命為徵南大將軍，率師駐杭州。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Southern Expedition Commander-in-Chief and led the army stationed at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Southern Expedition Commander-in-Chief and encamped at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明魯王以海監國紹興，明將方國安營錢塘江東，亘二百裡。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Lu Yihairegented at Shaoxing; the Ming general Fang Guo'an encamped east of the Qiantang for two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Lu Yihairegented at Shaoxing while Fang Guo’an held the east bank of the Qiantang for two hundred li.

sentences.zh: 師無舟，會江沙暴漲，固山額真圖賴等督兵徑涉，國安驚遁，以海走台州。

translations.literal: The army had no boats; the river sand suddenly rose in flood; gushan ejen Tulai and others directed the troops to wade straight across; Guo'an fled in alarm and Yihairetreated to Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Without boats, they forded when the river shallows flooded; Tulai and others led the men across; Guo’an broke and fled, and Yihairetreated to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 師入紹興，進克金華，擊殺明蜀王盛濃等，再進克衢州，浙江平。

translations.literal: The army entered Shaoxing, advanced and took Jinhua, killed the Ming Prince of Shu Shengong and others, advanced again and took Quzhou, and Zhejiang was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They entered Shaoxing, took Jinhua, killed Prince Shu Shengong and others, then seized Quzhou and pacified Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 明唐王聿鍵據福建，博洛率師破仙霞關，克浦城、建寧、延平。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Tang Yujian held Fujian; Bolo led the army, broke Xianxia Pass, and took Pucheng, Jianning, and Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Tang Yujian held Fujian; Bolo forced Xianxia Pass and took Pucheng, Jianning, and Yanping.

sentences.zh: 聿鍵走汀州，遣阿濟格、尼堪、努山等率師從之，克汀州，擒聿鍵及曲陽王盛渡等。

translations.literal: Yujian fled to Tingzhou; Bolo dispatched Ajige, Nikhan, Nusan, and others to follow, took Tingzhou, and captured Yujian and Prince of Quyang Shengdu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yujian fled to Tingzhou; Bolo sent Ajige, Nikhan, and Nusan in pursuit, took the city, and captured Yujian, Prince of Quyang Shengdu, and their party.

sentences.zh: 明將薑正希以二萬人夜來襲，擊之卻，斬萬餘級。

translations.literal: The Ming general Jiang Zhengxi came with twenty thousand men in a night attack; they were beaten back and more than ten thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhengxi struck by night with twenty thousand men; Bolo threw him back and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 又破敵分水關，克崇安。

translations.literal: He again defeated the enemy at Fenshui Pass and took Chong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the enemy at Fenshui Pass and took Chong’an.

sentences.zh: 梅勒額真卓布泰等克福州，斬所置巡撫楊廷清等，降其將鄭芝龍等二百九十餘人、馬步兵十一萬有奇。

translations.literal: Meile ejen Zhuobutai and others took Fuzhou, beheaded the grand coordinator Yang Tingqing and others whom they had appointed, and received the surrender of their generals Zheng Zhilong and more than two hundred and ninety others, with infantry and cavalry numbering a hundred and ten thousand odd.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuobutai and others seized Fuzhou, executed the grand coordinator Yang Tingqing and his colleagues, and received Zheng Zhilong and nearly three hundred other officers with more than a hundred and ten thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 師復進，下興化、漳州、泉州諸府。

translations.literal: The army advanced again and took Xinghua, Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, and the other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The army pressed on and reduced Xinghua, Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣昂邦章京佟養甲徇廣東，克潮州、惠州、廣州，擊殺明唐王聿鍵及諸王世子十餘人，承製以養甲為兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he dispatched angbang janggin Tong Yangjia to sweep Guangdong, took Chaozhou, Huizhou, and Guangzhou, killed the Ming Prince of Tang Yujian and more than ten princely sons, and by imperial commission made Yangjia Governor-General of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent Tong Yangjia into Guangdong; Chaozhou, Huizhou, and Guangzhou fell; Yujian and more than ten princes were killed; Yangjia was commissioned governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 四年，師還，進封端重郡王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the army returned and he was advanced to Prince of the State of Duanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the army returned and he was raised to Prince of the State of Duanzhong.

sentences.zh: 五年，以所獲金幣、人口賚焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was rewarded with the gold, coins, and population captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was rewarded with the gold, coin, and captives taken in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 偕阿濟格防喀爾喀，徇大同，討叛將薑瓖。

translations.literal: Together with Ajige he guarded against the Khalkha, swept Datong, and campaigned against the rebel general Jiang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: With Ajige he watched the Khalkha, raided Datong, and marched against the rebel Jiang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，偕碩塞援代州，克其郛。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, together with Shose he relieved Daizhou and took its outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year he and Shose relieved Daizhou and took its suburbs.

sentences.zh: 三月，瓖將馬得勝以五千自北山逼我師，博洛率千餘騎應之，與巴牙喇纛章京鰲拜等奮擊，大破之，斬馘過半，瓖閉城不敢出。

translations.literal: In the third month Jiang Xiang's general Ma Desheng came from the northern hills with five thousand to press our army; Bolo led a little more than a thousand horsemen to meet them; together with banner commander Oboi and others he struck fiercely, routed them utterly, beheaded more than half, and Xiang closed the city and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Ma Desheng came down from the northern hills with five thousand men; Bolo met him with a thousand-odd horsemen, joined Oboi in a furious charge, cut down more than half the force, and Xiang shut himself in the city.

sentences.zh: 睿親王多爾袞自京師至軍議撫，承製進親王，命為定西大將軍。

translations.literal: Prince Regent Dorgon came from the capital to the army to discuss pacification, advanced him to prince by imperial commission, and appointed him Pacifier of the West Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Regent Dorgon came from Beijing to negotiate terms, promoted him to prince, and named him Pacifier of the West.

sentences.zh: 移師汾州，下清源、交城、文水、徐溝、祁諸縣，戰平陽、絳州；

translations.literal: He shifted the army to Fenzhou, took Qingyuan, Jiaocheng, Wenshui, Xugou, Qi, and the other counties, and fought at Pingyang and Jiangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He moved on Fenzhou, reduced Qingyuan, Jiaocheng, Wenshui, Xugou, Qi, and the other counties, and fought at Pingyang and Jiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 又遣軍克孝義，戰壽陽、平遙、遼州、榆次：屢捷。

translations.literal: He also dispatched troops to take Xiaoyi and fought at Shouyang, Pingyao, Liaozhou, and Yuci: repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: detached columns took Xiaoyi and won repeated victories at Shouyang, Pingyao, Liaozhou, and Yuci.

sentences.zh: 英親王阿濟格、敬謹親王尼堪圍大同，巽親王滿達海、謙郡王瓦克達定朔州、寧武。

translations.literal: Prince Ying Ajige and Prince Jingjin Nikhan invested Datong; Prince Xun Mandahai and Prince Qian Wakda secured Shuozhou and Ningwu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying Ajige and Prince Jingjin Nikhan besieged Datong; Prince Xun Mandahai and Prince Qian Wakda secured Shuozhou and Ningwu.

sentences.zh: 召博洛還京師，疏言：「太原、平陽、汾州所屬諸縣雖漸次收復，然未下者尚多，恐撤軍後，賊乘虛襲踞，請仍留守御。

translations.literal: Bolo was recalled to the capital and memorialized: "Although the counties subordinate to Taiyuan, Pingyang, and Fenzhou have been gradually recovered, many are still untaken; I fear that if the army withdraws the bandits will seize the chance to raid and hold them; I ask to remain on garrison duty."
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to Beijing, Bolo memorialized: “Though the counties of Taiyuan, Pingyang, and Fenzhou are coming in one by one, many strongholds remain; if we withdraw, the rebels may seize them again; I beg leave to stay and hold the line.”

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 瓖既誅，與滿達海合軍克汾州，復嵐、永寧二縣，戰絳州孟城驛、老君廟諸地，盡殲瓖餘黨，乃還師。

translations.literal: After Xiang was executed, together with Mandahai he combined armies and took Fenzhou, recovered Lan and Yongning counties, fought at Mengcheng post in Jiangzhou and Laojun Temple and other places, utterly destroyed Xiang's remaining partisans, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang was put to death, Bolo and Mandahai together retook Fenzhou, recovered Lan and Yongning, annihilated the remnant bands at Mengcheng post and Laojun Temple, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 七年，偕滿達海、尼堪同理六部事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, together with Mandahai and Nikhan, he jointly managed the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he shared supervision of the Six Ministries with Mandahai and Nikhan.

sentences.zh: 再坐事，降郡王。

translations.literal: Again convicted of an offense, he was reduced to prince of the second degree.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted again, he was demoted to a lesser princely rank.

sentences.zh: 世祖親政，復爵。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor took personal rule, his rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shunzhi Emperor assumed personal rule, his title was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋命掌戶部。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered to manage the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon put in charge of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，薨，謚曰定。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year he died; his posthumous title was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of the ninth year and was posthumously titled Ding.

sentences.zh: 子齊克新，襲。

translations.literal: His son Qikexin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qikexin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 十六年，追論博洛分多爾袞遺財，又掌戶部時尚書譚泰逞私攬權，不力阻，奪爵、謚，齊克新降貝勒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, on reconsideration, Bolo was charged with dividing Dorgon's estate; also, when he managed the Board of Revenue the minister Tan Tai abused his power for private ends and he did not firmly restrain him; his title and posthumous name were stripped and Qikexin was reduced to beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Bolo was posthumously condemned for sharing in Dorgon’s estate and for failing to curb Tan Tai’s abuses at Revenue; his honors were revoked and Qikexin was reduced to beile.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，謚懷思。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died; his posthumous title was Huaisi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year with the posthumous title Huaisi.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the title was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir and the line ended.

sentences.zh: 博洛子塔爾納封郡王，卒，謚敏思。

translations.literal: Bolo's son Tarna was enfeoffed as prince of the second degree; when he died his posthumous title was Minsi.
translations.idiomatic: Bolo’s son Tarna had been made a prince of the second degree; at his death he was titled Minsi.

sentences.zh: 坐博洛罪，追奪爵。

translations.literal: On account of Bolo's crime his title was posthumously stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Bolo’s disgrace his honors were posthumously revoked.

sentences.zh: 悼愍貝子蘇布圖，阿巴泰孫。

translations.literal: Beizi Daomin Subutu was Abatai's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Subutu, posthumously Beizi Daomin, was a grandson of Abatai.

sentences.zh: 父尚建，追封貝子，謚賢愨。

translations.literal: His father Shangjian was posthumously enfeoffed as beizi with the posthumous title Xianque.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shangjian was posthumously made beizi with the title Xianque.

sentences.zh: 蘇布圖初封輔國公。

translations.literal: Subutu was first enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Subutu was first enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，從勒克德渾駐江寧，移師徵湖廣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he followed Lekdehun in garrisoning Jiangning and shifted the army to campaign in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he followed Lekdehun to garrison Jiangning, then marched into Huguang.

sentences.zh: 三年，從定荊州、襄陽有功，賜金五十、銀千，進貝子。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed in securing Jingzhou and Xiangyang with merit, was granted fifty taels of gold and a thousand taels of silver, and was advanced to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he helped secure Jingzhou and Xiangyang, received fifty taels of gold and a thousand of silver, and was raised to beizi.

sentences.zh: 五年，復從濟爾哈朗徇湖廣，卒於軍，謚悼愍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again followed Jirhalang in sweeping Huguang and died in the army; his posthumous title was Daomin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again campaigned in Huguang under Jirhalang and died on campaign; he was posthumously titled Daomin.

sentences.zh: 子顏齡，封鎮國公。

translations.literal: His son Yanling was enfeoffed as Prince of the State Who Guards the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanling was made Prince of the State Who Guards the Realm.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the title was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir and the line ended.

sentences.zh: 蘇布圖弟強度，封貝子，謚介潔，亦不襲。

translations.literal: Subutu's younger brother Qiangdu was enfeoffed as beizi with the posthumous title Jiejie; he too left no heir.
translations.idiomatic: Subutu’s younger brother Qiangdu was made beizi with the posthumous title Jiejie; his line also died out.

sentences.zh: 鎮國恪僖公巴布泰，太祖第九子。

translations.literal: Duke of the State Who Guards the Realm Kejie Gong Babutai was the Taizu Emperor's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Babutai, posthumously Duke of the State Who Guards the Realm Kejie, was the ninth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 天命十年，偕阿拜、塔拜伐東海北路呼爾哈部，有功。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianming, together with Abai and Tabai he campaigned against the Hurha of the northern Eastern Sea route and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 10 he joined Abai and Tabai against the Hurha of the northern Eastern Sea route and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 十一年，命理正黃旗事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was ordered to manage the affairs of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was put in charge of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 天聰四年，從阿敏駐永平。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancong he followed Amin in garrisoning Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 4 he followed Amin to garrison Yongping.

sentences.zh: 明兵攻灤州，巴布泰不能御，坐罷。

translations.literal: Ming troops attacked Luanzhou; Babutai could not repel them and was dismissed for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming forces attacked Luanzhou he failed to hold them off and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 八年，授梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed meile ejen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed meile ejen.

sentences.zh: 從伐明，克保全州。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Ming and took Baoquan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against the Ming and took Baoquan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 巴布泰匿所獲不以聞，復坐罷。

translations.literal: Babutai concealed what he had captured and did not report it; he was again dismissed for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: He hid his spoils and failed to report them; he was dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 崇德六年，授三等奉國將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongde he was granted third-rank fengguo jiangjun.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 6 he was granted third-rank fengguo jiangjun.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關，逐李自成至慶都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed in entering the Pass and pursued Li Zicheng to Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he followed the army through the Pass and pursued Li Zicheng to Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 二年，進一等。

translations.literal: In the second year he was advanced to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to first rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，從勒克德渾伐湖廣，戰安遠、南漳、西峰口、關王嶺、襄陽，屢破敵。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Lekdehun in campaigning against Huguang, fought at Anyuan, Nanzhang, Xifengkou, Guanwangling, and Xiangyang, and repeatedly defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Lekdehun into Huguang, fought at Anyuan, Nanzhang, Xifengkou, Guanwangling, and Xiangyang, and repeatedly routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 四年，進輔國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced to Duke Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Duke Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 六年，偕務達海討薑瓖，進鎮國公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, together with Wudahai, he campaigned against Jiang Xiang and was advanced to Duke Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined Wudahai against Jiang Xiang and was raised to Duke Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，卒，予謚。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year he died and was granted a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year he died and received a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子噶布喇，封輔國公；

translations.literal: His son Gabula was enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo;
translations.idiomatic: His son Gabula was enfeoffed as Duke Fuguo;

sentences.zh: 祜錫祿，襲三等鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: Husilu inherited the third-rank Prince Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: Husilu inherited the third-rank Prince Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 其後並以奉恩將軍世襲。

translations.literal: Thereafter all lines inherited by feng'en jiangjun in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all lines held feng'en jiangjun in perpetual succession.

sentences.zh: 德格類，太祖第十子。

translations.literal: Degede was the Taizu Emperor's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Degede was the tenth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 初授台吉。

translations.literal: He was first granted the rank of taiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was first granted the rank of taiji.

sentences.zh: 天命六年，師略奉集堡，將還，有一卒指明兵所在，德格類偕岳託、碩託進擊之，擊敗明將李秉誠。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianming the army raided Fengji Fort; as they were about to return, a soldier pointed out where the Ming troops were; Degede together with Yueto and Shuoto advanced to attack and defeated the Ming general Li Bingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 6 the army raided Fengji Fort. As they were about to withdraw, a soldier pointed out the Ming position; Degede joined Yueto and Shuoto in an attack and defeated the Ming general Li Bingcheng.

sentences.zh: 復偕台吉寨桑古閱三岔河橋，至海州，城中官民張樂舁輿迎德格類等，令軍士毋擾民，毋奪財物，毋宿城上，毋入民居。

translations.literal: Again together with taiji Zaisanggu he inspected the Sancha River bridge and reached Haizhou; officials and people in the city welcomed Degede and the others with music and palanquins; he ordered the troops not to disturb the people, not to seize property, not to lodge on the city wall, and not to enter private dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined taiji Zaisanggu to inspect the Sancha River bridge and went on to Haizhou, where officials and townspeople welcomed Degede and his party with music and palanquins. He ordered his soldiers not to harass the people, seize goods, camp on the walls, or enter private homes.

sentences.zh: 翌日，遣視三岔河者還報橋毀無舟楫，乃還。

translations.literal: The next day those sent to reconnoiter the Sancha River returned and reported that the bridge was destroyed and there were no boats; they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next day scouts sent to the Sancha River reported the bridge destroyed and no boats available, so they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕阿巴泰伐喀爾喀紥嚕特部。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Abatai, he campaigned against the Khalkha Jarud tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined Abatai against the Khalkha Jarud tribe.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復從代善伐紥嚕特部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he again followed Daishan in campaigning against the Jarud tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he again followed Daishan against the Jarud tribe.

sentences.zh: 天聰三年，偕濟爾哈朗略錦州，焚其積聚。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancong, together with Jirhalang, he raided Jinzhou and burned its stores.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 3 he joined Jirhalang in raiding Jinzhou and burning its granaries.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進和碩貝勒。

translations.literal: His merit was recognized and he was advanced to Prince of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was raised to Prince of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，初設六部，掌戶部事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Six Ministries were first established; he managed the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when the Six Ministries were first established, he took charge of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 從圍大凌河，德格類率師策應，擊破明監軍道張春。

translations.literal: In besieging Dalinghe, Degede led troops in support and defeated the Ming supervising censor Zhang Chun.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Dalinghe, Degede led supporting troops and routed the Ming supervising censor Zhang Chun.

sentences.zh: 十月，祖大壽降，偕阿巴泰等偽為明軍襲錦州，擊斬甚眾。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Zu Dashou surrendered; together with Abatai and others he disguised themselves as Ming troops and raided Jinzhou, killing a great many.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, after Zu Dashou surrendered, he joined Abatai and others in Ming disguise to raid Jinzhou and killed a great many.

sentences.zh: 六年，偕濟爾哈朗等略歸化城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, together with Jirhalang and others, he raided Guihua City.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined Jirhalang and others in raiding Guihua City.

sentences.zh: 復偕岳託略地，自耀州至蓋州迤南。

translations.literal: Again together with Yueto he raided territory from Yaozhou south to Gaizhou and beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Again with Yueto he raided from Yaozhou south through Gaizhou and beyond.

sentences.zh: 七年，攻剋旅順口。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he stormed and took Lüshunkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he stormed Lüshunkou.

sentences.zh: 八年，從伐明，撫定蒙古來歸人戶。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed the campaign against the Ming and pacified the households of Mongols who had come over.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined the Ming campaign and settled the households of Mongols who had submitted.

sentences.zh: 克獨石口。

translations.literal: He took Dushikou.
translations.idiomatic: He took Dushikou.

sentences.zh: 攻赤城，未拔。

translations.literal: He attacked Chicheng but did not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Chicheng but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 入保全州，會師應州，還。

translations.literal: He entered Baoquan Prefecture, joined forces at Yingzhou, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Baoquan Prefecture, united with the main force at Yingzhou, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 九年十月，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the ninth year he died.

sentences.zh: 上臨其喪，痛悼之，漏盡三鼓乃還。

translations.literal: The emperor attended his funeral and grieved deeply, not returning until the third watch when the water clock had run dry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended his funeral and mourned deeply, not returning until the third watch when the clepsydra had run dry.

sentences.zh: 設幄坐其中，撤饌三日。

translations.literal: A pavilion was set up for him to sit within, and feasts were withdrawn for three days.
translations.idiomatic: A mourning pavilion was erected for him to sit in, and court feasts were suspended for three days.

sentences.zh: 逾月，莽古爾泰既卒，為冷僧機所訐，以大逆削籍，德格類坐同謀，追削貝勒。

translations.literal: More than a month later, after Manggūltai had died, Lengsenji accused him of treason and he was stripped from the registers; Degede was convicted as co-conspirator and his princedom was posthumously stripped.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, after Manggūltai's death, Lengsenji denounced him for treason and he was expunged from the registers; Degede was judged a co-conspirator and stripped of his princedom posthumously.

sentences.zh: 子鄧什庫，並坐，削宗籍；

translations.literal: His son Dengshiku was implicated, stripped from the clan registers;
translations.idiomatic: His son Dengshiku was implicated and struck from the clan registers;

sentences.zh: 德克西克，以侍衛從豪格徵張獻忠，戰死，世祖詔其子輝爾食一等阿思哈尼哈番俸。

translations.literal: Dekesike, as an imperial bodyguard, followed Hooge in campaigning against Zhang Xianzhong and died in battle; the Shizu Emperor ordered his son Huier to receive the salary of a first-rank ashahaniha fan.
translations.idiomatic: Dekesike served as an imperial bodyguard under Hooge against Zhang Xianzhong and fell in battle; the Shizu Emperor granted his son Huier the stipend of a first-rank ashahaniha fan.

sentences.zh: 子五，雲柱，授一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Yunzhu was granted a first-rank adaha fan.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons; Yunzhu was granted a first-rank adaha fan.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年，聖祖命復宗籍，賜紅帶。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi the Shengzu Emperor ordered restoration to the clan registers and granted a red sash.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 52 the Shengzu Emperor restored them to the clan registers and granted the red sash.

sentences.zh: 巴布海，太祖第十一子。

translations.literal: Babuhai was the Taizu Emperor's eleventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Babuhai was the eleventh son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 初授牛錄章京。

translations.literal: He was first appointed niru janggin.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed niru janggin.

sentences.zh: 天聰八年，授一等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he was appointed first-rank jalan janggin.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 8 he was appointed first-rank jalan janggin.

sentences.zh: 嘗命偕鎮國將軍阿拜祭陵，巴布海不待阿拜，先往祭。

translations.literal: He was once ordered to perform the tomb sacrifice together with Prince Zhenguo Abai; Babuhai did not wait for Abai and went first to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He was once ordered to perform the tomb rites with Prince Zhenguo Abai, but Babuhai did not wait for Abai and went ahead to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 牛未至，取民牛代，以祭牛償民，民以小不受，訟焉，罰銀三十償民，又不與，再訟。

translations.literal: The sacrificial ox had not arrived; he took a commoner's ox in its place; he compensated the people with the sacrificial ox, but they regarded it as inferior and would not accept it, and sued; he was fined thirty taels of silver to compensate the people, yet did not pay, and they sued again.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrificial ox had not arrived he took a villager's ox instead, then offered the sacrificial ox in compensation; the owners deemed it inferior and refused it, and sued. He was fined thirty taels to compensate them but still would not pay, and they sued again.

sentences.zh: 巴布海聞上，上責其愚黯，且謂其受制於妻，妻，揚古利女也。

translations.literal: Babuhai reported to the emperor; the emperor rebuked him for stupidity and dullness, and said further that he was controlled by his wife—his wife was Yangguli's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Babuhai appealed to the emperor, who rebuked his folly and obtuseness and said he was ruled by his wife—Yangguli's daughter.

sentences.zh: 崇德四年，授梅勒額真，封鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongde he was appointed meile ejen and enfeoffed as Prince Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 4 he was appointed meile ejen and enfeoffed as Prince Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 七年，巴布海語固山額真譚泰曰：「原罷我梅勒額真。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Babuhai said to gushan ejen Tan Tai: "I wish to resign my meile ejen post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Babuhai told gushan ejen Tan Tai, "I wish to give up my meile ejen post.

sentences.zh: 堪為梅勒額真者，多於草木！

translations.literal: Those fit to be meile ejen are more numerous than plants and trees!
translations.idiomatic: Men fit to be meile ejen outnumber the grass and trees!"

sentences.zh: 」譚泰語折之，誓曰：「若口與心違者，天日鑒之！

translations.literal: " Tan Tai rebutted him in speech and swore: "If my mouth contradicts my heart, may Heaven and the sun bear witness!
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai answered him sharply and swore, "If my words belie my heart, may Heaven and sun be witness!"

sentences.zh: 」圖海奉命差擇牛錄貧富，巴布海曰：「我所領牛錄甚富。

translations.literal: " Tuhai was ordered to assess the wealth of niru; Babuhai said: "The niru I command is very rich.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhai was ordered to assess niru wealth; Babuhai said, "The niru under me is very rich."

sentences.zh: 」語聞，巴布海曰：「我非太祖之子歟？

translations.literal: " When word reached him, Babuhai said: "Am I not a son of the Taizu Emperor?
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported, Babuhai said, "Am I not the Taizu Emperor's son?

sentences.zh: 譚泰等顧厚誣我。

translations.literal: Tan Tai and the others only seek to slander me thickly.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Tai and the rest only mean to heap false charges on me."

sentences.zh: 」廷鞫皆實，罪當死，上寬之，但奪爵。

translations.literal: " At court interrogation all was found true; the penalty was death; the emperor showed mercy and only stripped his rank.
translations.idiomatic: At trial all proved true; the penalty was death, but the emperor spared him and only stripped his rank.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，有為飛書訐譚泰者，投一等公塔瞻第。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor took the throne, someone wrote a flying petition denouncing Tan Tai and cast it into the residence of the first-rank duke Tazhan.
translations.idiomatic: At the Shizu Emperor's accession, an anonymous denunciation of Tan Tai was thrown into the mansion of the first-rank duke Tazhan.

sentences.zh: 鞫其僕，謂得之巴布海家。

translations.literal: His servants were interrogated and said it had come from Babuhai's household.
translations.idiomatic: Under interrogation his servants said it came from Babuhai's household.

sentences.zh: 內監逮訊，不承，巴布海及其妻並子阿喀喇皆坐死，籍其家予譚泰。

translations.literal: The inner court arrested and questioned them; they would not confess; Babuhai, his wife, and his son Akala were all sentenced to death, and their property was registered and given to Tan Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Palace agents seized and questioned them; they would not confess. Babuhai, his wife, and his son Akala were all put to death, and their estate was confiscated and given to Tan Tai.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，譚泰誅，乃以其孥及遺產畀巴布泰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi Tan Tai was executed, and his family and remaining property were then given to Babutai.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9, after Tan Tai was executed, his dependents and remaining property were turned over to Babutai.

sentences.zh: 阿濟格，太祖第十二子。

translations.literal: Ajige was the Taizu Emperor's twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Ajige was the twelfth son of the Taizu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 初授台吉。

translations.literal: He was first granted the rank of taiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was first granted the rank of taiji.

sentences.zh: 天命十年，從貝勒莽古爾泰伐察哈爾，至農安塔。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianming he followed Prince Manggūltai in campaigning against the Chahar, reaching Nong'an Tower.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianming 10 he followed Prince Manggūltai against the Chahar as far as Nong'an Tower.

sentences.zh: 十一年，偕台吉碩託伐喀爾喀巴林部，復從貝勒代善伐紥魯特，皆有功，授貝勒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, together with taiji Shuoto, he campaigned against the Khalkha Bairin tribe, and again followed Prince Daishan against the Jarud—all with merit; he was granted the rank of beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he joined taiji Shuoto against the Khalkha Bairin and again followed Prince Daishan against the Jarud, distinguishing himself each time, and was granted beile rank.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，偕貝勒阿敏伐北韓，克五城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong, together with Prince Amin, he campaigned against Korea and took five cities.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 1 he joined Prince Amin against Korea and took five cities.

sentences.zh: 從上伐明，偕莽古爾泰衛塔山糧運。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor in campaigning against the Ming; together with Manggūltai he guarded grain transport at Tashan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor against the Ming and, with Manggūltai, guarded grain transport at Tashan.

sentences.zh: 會師錦州，薄寧遠，明兵千餘人為車營，掘壕，前列火器，阿濟格擊殲之。

translations.literal: The army united at Jinzhou and pressed Ningyuan; more than a thousand Ming troops formed a wagon encampment, dug trenches, and arrayed firearms in front; Ajige attacked and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: The army united at Jinzhou and pressed Ningyuan. Over a thousand Ming troops formed a wagon fort, dug trenches, and lined up firearms in front; Ajige attacked and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 總兵滿桂出城陣，上欲進擊，諸貝勒以距城近，諫不可，獨阿濟格請從。

translations.literal: General Man Gui deployed in battle outside the city; the emperor wished to advance and attack; the beile, because they were close to the city, admonished that it was not permissible; only Ajige asked to follow.
translations.idiomatic: General Man Gui drew up outside the city. The emperor meant to attack, but the beile, citing the nearness of the walls, urged against it; only Ajige asked to go with him.

sentences.zh: 上督阿濟格馳擊明騎兵至城下，諸貝勒皆慚，奮不及胄，亦進擊其步軍，明兵死者大半。

translations.literal: The emperor urged Ajige to charge and attack the Ming cavalry to the foot of the wall; the beile were all shamed, fought without even donning armor, and also advanced against the infantry; more than half the Ming troops died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spurred Ajige to charge the Ming horse to the foot of the wall. Shamed, the other beile fought without even buckling on armor and joined the assault on the infantry; more than half the Ming force perished.

sentences.zh: 二年，以擅主弟多鐸婚，削爵，尋復之。

translations.literal: In the second year, for presiding over his younger brother Dodo's marriage on his own authority, his rank was stripped; shortly afterward it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was stripped of rank for arranging his younger brother Dodo's marriage on his own authority, but soon had it restored.

sentences.zh: 三年，偕濟爾哈朗略明錦州、寧遠，焚其積聚，俘三千。

translations.literal: In the third year, together with Jirhalang, he raided Ming Jinzhou and Ningyuan, burned their stores, and took three thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined Jirhalang in raiding Jinzhou and Ningyuan, burned their stores, and took three thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 復從上伐明，克龍井關，下漢兒莊城，克洪山口。

translations.literal: Again he followed the emperor in campaigning against the Ming, took Longjing Pass, reduced Han'erzhuang city, and took Hongshan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Again he followed the emperor against the Ming, took Longjing Pass, reduced Han'erzhuang, and seized Hongshan Pass.

sentences.zh: 進次遵化，擊斬明總兵趙率教。

translations.literal: Advancing to Zunhua, he struck down the Ming commander Zhao Shuaijiao.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Zunhua, he killed the Ming commander Zhao Shuaijiao.

sentences.zh: 薄明都，袁崇煥、祖大壽以兵二萬赴援，屯廣渠門外，師逐之，迫壕，阿濟格馬創，乃還。

translations.literal: Pressing the Ming capital, Yuan Chonghuan and Zu Dashou came with twenty thousand men to relieve; they encamped outside Guangqu Gate; the army pursued them, pressing them to the moat; Ajige's horse was wounded and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the Ming capital, Yuan Chonghuan and Zu Dashou marched twenty thousand men to relieve it and camped outside Guangqu Gate. Our army pursued them to the moat; Ajige's horse was wounded and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋偕阿巴泰等略通州，至張家灣。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, together with Abatai and others, he raided Tongzhou as far as Zhangjiawan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, with Abatai and others, he raided Tongzhou as far as Zhangjiawan.

sentences.zh: 尋從上閱薊州，遇明山海關援兵，阿濟格偕代善突入敵陣，大破之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again followed the emperor in reviewing Jizhou; encountering Ming reinforcements from Shanhai Pass, Ajige together with Daishan burst into the enemy formation and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the emperor to Jizhou, met Ming reinforcements from Shanhai Pass, and with Daishan charged into their ranks and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 四年，復從伐明，趨廣寧，會師大凌河。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again followed in campaigning against the Ming, advanced toward Guangning, and united with the army at Dalinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again campaigned against the Ming, marched toward Guangning, and united with the main force at Dalinghe.

sentences.zh: 夜圍錦州，明兵襲阿濟格營，霧不見人，阿濟格嚴陣待。

translations.literal: At night they besieged Jinzhou; Ming troops raided Ajige's camp; in the fog one could not see people; Ajige held the formation and waited.
translations.idiomatic: By night they besieged Jinzhou. Ming troops raided Ajige's camp; in the fog men could not see one another; Ajige held his ranks and waited.

sentences.zh: 青氣降，霧豁若門闢，急縱擊，獲明裨將一、甲械及馬二百餘。

translations.literal: Green vapor descended; the fog opened as if a gate were thrown wide; he charged swiftly and took one Ming deputy commander, armor and weapons, and more than two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Green mist fell and the fog parted as if a gate had opened; he charged hard, capturing a Ming deputy commander, arms and armor, and more than two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 上酌金卮親勞之，授圍城方略。

translations.literal: The emperor poured wine from a golden goblet and personally rewarded him, conferring strategy for siege warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor poured wine from a golden cup and personally honored him, teaching him the art of siege.

sentences.zh: 尋聞明增兵，上命揚古利率八旗巴牙喇兵之半以益軍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, hearing that the Ming were reinforcing, the emperor ordered Yangguli to lead half the Eight Banners' bayara troops to reinforce the army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, learning the Ming were reinforcing, the emperor sent Yangguli with half the Eight Banners' bayara to strengthen the army.

sentences.zh: 大壽弟大弼逐我軍中偵騎近上前，上擐甲與戰，阿濟格馳至，明兵步騎遝出，奮擊卻之，斬明裨將一。

translations.literal: Dashou's younger brother Dabi pursued our scouts close to where the emperor was; the emperor donned armor and fought; Ajige galloped up; Ming infantry and cavalry poured out in succession; he fought fiercely and drove them back, beheading one Ming deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou's younger brother Dabi chased our scouts near the emperor's position. The emperor donned armor and fought; Ajige galloped up as Ming foot and horse poured forth; he fought fiercely, drove them back, and beheaded a Ming deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 上以所統兵付阿濟格，明監軍道張春援至，又戰於大凌河，截殺過半，逐北四十里。

translations.literal: The emperor entrusted the troops he commanded to Ajige; the Ming supervising censor Zhang Chun arrived in relief; they fought again at Dalinghe, cutting down more than half, and pursued north forty li.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor placed his own command under Ajige. When the Ming supervising censor Zhang Chun came to relieve the city, they fought again at Dalinghe, cut down more than half, and pursued forty li north.

sentences.zh: 六年，從伐察哈爾，林丹汗遁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed in campaigning against the Chahar; Lin Dan Khan fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the campaign against the Chahar; Lin Dan Khan fled.

sentences.zh: 上移師伐明，令阿濟格統左翼及蒙古兵略大同、宣府，盡得張家口所貯犒邊財物。

translations.literal: The emperor shifted the army to campaign against the Ming and ordered Ajige to command the Left Wing and Mongol troops to raid Datong and Xuanfu, seizing all the stores of border-reward goods at Zhangjiakou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned the army against the Ming and ordered Ajige to lead the Left Wing and Mongol forces against Datong and Xuanfu, seizing all the border-reward stores at Zhangjiakou.

sentences.zh: 七年，城通遠堡，迎降將孔有德，拒明及北韓兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year they fortified Tongyuan Fort, welcomed the surrendered general Kong Youde, and repelled Ming and Korean troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year they fortified Tongyuan Fort, received the defector Kong Youde, and repelled Ming and Korean forces.

sentences.zh: 詔問攻明及北韓、察哈爾三者何先，阿濟格言當攻明。

translations.literal: An edict asked which should come first—attacking the Ming, Korea, or the Chahar; Ajige said the Ming should be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Asked whether to strike the Ming, Korea, or the Chahar first, Ajige said the Ming should come first.

sentences.zh: 偕阿巴泰略山海關，詔責其不深入，阿濟格言；

translations.literal: Together with Abatai he raided Shanhai Pass; an edict rebuked him for not penetrating deeply; Ajige said:
translations.idiomatic: With Abatai he raided Shanhai Pass; rebuked for not pushing deep enough, Ajige replied:

sentences.zh: 「臣欲息馬候糧，諸貝勒不從。

translations.literal: "Your subject wished to rest the horses and await grain; the beile would not assent."
translations.idiomatic: "I wished to rest the horses and wait for grain, but the beile would not agree."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「汝果堅不還，諸貝勒將棄汝行乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If you had truly insisted on not returning, would the beile have abandoned you and marched away?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If you had truly refused to return, would the beile have left you and marched on?"

sentences.zh: 」八年，從伐明，克保全，拔靈丘。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed in campaigning against the Ming, took Baoquan, and stormed Lingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he campaigned against the Ming, took Baoquan, and stormed Lingqiu.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，進武英郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he was advanced to Prince of the Commandery of Wuying.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he was raised to Prince of the Commandery of Wuying.

sentences.zh: 偕饒餘貝勒阿巴泰及揚古利伐明，自雕鶚堡入長安嶺，薄延慶。

translations.literal: Together with Prince Raoyu Abatai and Yangguli he campaigned against the Ming, entering from Diaoge Fort through Chang'anling, pressing Yanqing.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Raoyu Abatai and Yangguli he marched against the Ming from Diaoge Fort through Chang'anling toward Yanqing.

sentences.zh: 越保定至安州，克昌平、定興、安肅、寶坻、東安、雄、順義、容城、文安諸縣，五十六戰皆捷，俘人畜十餘萬。

translations.literal: Passing Baoding to reach Anzhou, he took the prefectures and counties of Changping, Dingxing, Ansu, Baodi, Dong'an, Xiong, Shunyi, Rongcheng, and Wen'an; in fifty-six engagements all were victorious, capturing people and livestock numbering more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He passed Baoding to Anzhou and took Changping, Dingxing, Ansu, Baodi, Dong'an, Xiong, Shunyi, Rongcheng, Wen'an, and other counties—fifty-six battles, all won, with captives and livestock exceeding a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 又遣固山額真譚泰等設伏，斬遵化三屯營守將，獲馬百四十餘。

translations.literal: He also dispatched gushan ejen Tan Tai and others to set an ambush and behead the defending commander of Zunhua's Santunying, seizing more than a hundred and forty horses.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent gushan ejen Tan Tai and others to ambush and kill the garrison commander of Zunhua's Santunying, taking more than a hundred and forty horses.

sentences.zh: 得優旨，賜鞍馬一。

translations.literal: He received an edict of praise and was granted one saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: He received a commendatory edict and was granted one saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 師還，上迎勞地載門外十里，見阿濟格勞瘠，為淚下，親酌金卮勞之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the emperor welcomed and rewarded them ten li outside Dizai Gate; seeing Ajige gaunt and worn, he wept, and personally poured wine from a golden goblet to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the emperor met them ten li beyond Dizai Gate; seeing Ajige worn thin, he wept and personally poured wine from a golden cup to honor him.

sentences.zh: 上伐北韓，命守牛莊。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned against Korea and ordered him to guard Niuzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Korea he ordered Ajige to hold Niuzhuang.

sentences.zh: 二年，碩託攻皮島未下，阿濟格督所部水陸併進，克之。

translations.literal: In the second year Shuoto attacked Pidao but did not take it; Ajige directed his command to advance by land and water together and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Shuoto besieged Pidao without success; Ajige led his forces by land and sea together and took it.

sentences.zh: 上遣使褒勞。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys to praise and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to praise and reward him.

sentences.zh: 四年，從伐明，阿濟格揚言欲以紅衣炮攻台，守者懼，四里屯、張剛屯、寶林寺、旺民屯、於家屯、成化峪、道爾彰諸台俱下。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed in campaigning against the Ming; Ajige proclaimed that he would attack the forts with red-barrel cannon; the defenders were afraid, and the forts at Silidun, Zhanggangtun, Baolin Temple, Wangmintun, Yujiatun, Chenghuayu, Daoerzhang, and others all fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he campaigned against the Ming. Ajige declared he would batter the forts with red-barrel guns; the garrisons were terrified, and Silidun, Zhanggangtun, Baolin Temple, Wangmintun, Yujiatun, Chenghuayu, Daoerzhang, and other forts all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 尋還守塔山、連山，俘人馬千計。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he returned to guard Tashan and Lianshan, capturing people and horses numbering a thousand odd.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he returned to hold Tashan and Lianshan, taking a thousand-odd people and horses.

sentences.zh: 復偕阿巴泰略錦州、寧遠。

translations.literal: Again together with Abatai he raided Jinzhou and Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Again with Abatai he raided Jinzhou and Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 六年，偕濟爾哈朗圍錦州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, together with Jirhalang, he besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined Jirhalang in besieging Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 守郛蒙古台吉吳巴什等議舉城降，祖大壽覺之，擊蒙古兵，阿濟格夜登陴助戰，明兵敗，徙蒙古降者於義州。

translations.literal: The Mongol taiji defending the outer wall, Wubashi and others, plotted to surrender the city; Zu Dashou detected it and attacked the Mongol troops; Ajige climbed the battlements by night to assist in the fighting; the Ming troops were defeated; the Mongol who had surrendered were moved to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol taiji on the outer wall, Wubashi and others, plotted to hand over the city. Zu Dashou discovered it and struck the Mongols; Ajige scaled the ramparts by night to aid the fight; the Ming were beaten back and the surrendering Mongols were relocated to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 屢擊敗明兵，賜銀四千。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated Ming troops and was rewarded with four thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly defeated Ming forces and was rewarded with four thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 洪承疇率諸將王樸、吳三桂等援錦州，號十三萬。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou led the generals Wang Pu, Wu Sangui, and others to relieve Jinzhou, claiming one hundred thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou led Wang Pu, Wu Sangui, and other generals to relieve Jinzhou with a force said to number one hundred thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 上親視師，營松山。

translations.literal: The sovereign personally inspected the army and encamped at Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally inspected the army and encamped at Songshan.

sentences.zh: 明兵奔塔山，阿濟格追擊之，獲筆架山積粟，又偕多爾袞克敵台四，擒明將王希賢等，樸、三桂僅以身免。

translations.literal: Ming troops fled toward Tashan; Ajige pursued them, seized the grain stored on Bijia Mountain, and together with Dorgon took four enemy forts, capturing the Ming generals Wang Xixian and others; Pu and Sangui barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming force fled toward Tashan. Ajige pursued them, seized the grain stored on Bijia Mountain, and with Dorgon captured four enemy forts and the Ming generals Wang Xixian and others; Wang Pu and Wu Sangui barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 明兵猶守錦州、松山、杏山、高橋諸地，上還盛京，命阿濟格偕杜度、多鐸等圍之。

translations.literal: Ming troops still held Jinzhou, Songshan, Xingshan, Gaoqiao, and other places; the sovereign returned to Mukden and ordered Ajige together with Duodu, Dodo, and others to invest them.
translations.idiomatic: Ming forces still held Jinzhou, Songshan, Xingshan, Gaoqiao, and other places. The emperor returned to Mukden and ordered Ajige, Duodu, Dodo, and others to besiege them.

sentences.zh: 承疇夜出松山襲我軍，阿濟格等督眾環射之，明兵敗還，城閉不得入，其眾二千皆降。

translations.literal: Chengchou made a night sortie from Songshan against our army; Ajige and others directed the troops to shoot around them; the Ming army was defeated and turned back but could not enter the city when the gates were shut, and their two thousand men all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou made a night sortie from Songshan against our camp. Ajige and the others had the troops shoot in all directions; the Ming force was beaten back but could not re-enter the city when the gates were closed, and two thousand men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 七年，圍杏山，遣軍略寧遠。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he invested Xingshan and detached troops to raid Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he besieged Xingshan and sent detachments to raid Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 三桂以四千人駐塔山、高橋，不戰而退，縱兵四擊，又迭敗之。

translations.literal: Sangui stationed four thousand men at Tashan and Gaoqiao, withdrew without fighting, and our troops struck in four directions and defeated them again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui posted four thousand men at Tashan and Gaoqiao, withdrew without fighting, and our troops attacked on four sides and defeated them repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 八年，復偕濟爾哈朗攻寧遠，軍城北，布雲梯發炮，城圮，克之；

translations.literal: In the eighth year he again joined Jirhalang in attacking Ningyuan, encamped north of the city, set up scaling ladders and opened fire with cannon; the wall collapsed and the city was taken;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he again joined Jirhalang in attacking Ningyuan, encamped north of the city, deployed scaling ladders and opened fire with cannon, breached the wall, and took the city;

sentences.zh: 抵前屯衛，攻城西，斬馘四千餘，明總兵黃色棄城遁，復克之。

translations.literal: reaching Qianjin garrison, he attacked the west of the city, beheaded more than four thousand, the Ming commander Huang Se abandoned the city and fled, and it was taken again.
translations.idiomatic: He then reached Qianjin garrison, attacked the west of the city, killed more than four thousand, the Ming commander Huang Se abandoned the city and fled, and it was captured again.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關破李自成，進英親王，賜鞍馬二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the entry through the passes, defeated Li Zicheng, was advanced to Prince Ying, and was given two saddle horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he followed the army through the passes, defeated Li Zicheng, was raised to Prince Ying, and was given two saddle horses.

sentences.zh: 命為靖遠大將軍，自邊外入陝西，斷自成歸路，八戰皆勝，克城四，降城三十八。

translations.literal: He was appointed Pacification Commissioner General for the Distant Regions, entered Shaanxi from beyond the frontier, cut off Zicheng's line of retreat, won eight battles, took four cities, and received the surrender of thirty-eight cities.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Pacification Commissioner General for the Distant Regions, entered Shaanxi from beyond the frontier, cut off Zicheng's retreat, won eight battles, took four cities, and received the surrender of thirty-eight cities.

sentences.zh: 時自成為多鐸所敗，棄西安走商州。

translations.literal: At that time Zicheng had been defeated by Dodo, abandoned Xi'an, and fled toward Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zicheng had been defeated by Dodo, abandoned Xi'an, and fled toward Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔多鐸趨淮、揚，而命阿濟格率師討自成。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dodo to hurry to the Huai and Yang regions while Ajige was ordered to lead troops against Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Dodo to hurry to the Huai and Yang regions while Ajige was ordered to lead troops against Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 自成南走，眾尚二十萬，規取南京。

translations.literal: Zicheng fled south; his followers still numbered two hundred thousand and planned to take Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng fled south with some two hundred thousand followers still at his command, intending to seize Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 阿濟格以師從之，及於鄧州，復南至承天、德安、武昌、富池口、桑家口、九江，屢破敵，自成走死，斬其將劉宗敏，俘宋獻策。

translations.literal: Ajige followed with his army, caught up at Dengzhou, then pressed south through Chengtian, De'an, Wuchang, Fuchikou, Sangjiakou, and Jiujiang, repeatedly defeating the enemy; Zicheng fled to his death, his general Liu Zongmin was beheaded, and Song Xiance was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Ajige pursued with his army, caught up at Dengzhou, then drove south through Chengtian, De'an, Wuchang, Fuchikou, Sangjiakou, and Jiujiang, winning repeated victories. Zicheng fled to his death; his general Liu Zongmin was beheaded and Song Xiance was captured.

sentences.zh: 宗敏，自成驍將；

translations.literal: Zongmin was Zicheng's fiercest general;
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin was Zicheng's fiercest general;

sentences.zh: 獻策，自成所倚任，號軍師者也。

translations.literal: Xiance was the man Zicheng relied on, known as his military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Xiance was the man Zicheng relied on and was known as his military adviser.

sentences.zh: 明將左良玉子夢庚方駐軍九江，師至，執總督袁繼咸等，率馬步兵十萬、舟數萬，詣軍門降。

translations.literal: The Ming general Zuo Menggeng, son of Zuo Liangyu, was then encamped at Jiujiang; when the army arrived he seized the governor Yuan Jixian and others and came to the camp gate to surrender with one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry and tens of thousands of boats.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming general Zuo Menggeng, son of Zuo Liangyu, was then stationed at Jiujiang. When the army arrived he seized Governor Yuan Jixian and others and came to the camp gate to surrender with one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry and tens of thousands of boats.

sentences.zh: 是役凡十三戰，下郡縣：河南十二，湖廣三十九，江西、江南皆六。

translations.literal: In this campaign there were thirteen battles in all and prefectures and counties were taken: twelve in Henan, thirty-nine in Huguang, and six each in Jiangxi and Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign there were thirteen battles in all; prefectures and counties taken numbered twelve in Henan, thirty-nine in Huguang, and six each in Jiangxi and Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，上使赴軍慰勞，詔曰：「王及行間將士馳驅跋涉，懸崖峻嶺，深江大河，萬有餘里，勞苦功高。

translations.literal: When victory was reported the sovereign sent envoys to the army to console them, with an edict saying: "The prince and the officers and soldiers on campaign have galloped and toiled over crags and cliffs and great rivers for more than ten thousand li, with arduous merit.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported the emperor sent envoys to console the army with an edict: "The prince and the officers and soldiers on campaign have galloped and toiled over crags and cliffs and great rivers for more than ten thousand li, with arduous merit.

sentences.zh: 寇氛既靖，宜即班師。
